Make JusPrin's "Your own API key" setup screen show whether a key is already saved, without revealing it. Repo: /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin. Work in your own new worktree off jusprin-newui. Kenneth approved the design on 2026-10-21.

## The design (source of truth: the Claude canvas artifact; Figma is retired)
Canvas "JusPrin v2", https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v, page "Agent Setup · Empty State", board agent-setup-api-key-saved-vs-empty-proposal.dc.html ("api-key-field · saved vs empty · proposal"). Read it with the Artifact tool (action "read", path "project/agent-setup-api-key-saved-vs-empty-proposal.dc.html"); it is next to the existing setup-api-key boards. Five states:
1. **No key saved.** The field shows only placeholder text, "Paste your Anthropic key (sk-ant-…)" in text-tertiary, never bullets; "Paste" sits inside the field; Check key is disabled.
2. **Key saved.** A check icon (status-success) with "Key saved on this computer". The key is shown read-only as its start plus last 4 characters ("sk-ant-…a3F9") in the code style at full contrast, on a surface-subtle field, with "Replace" and "Remove" (Remove in status-danger). Below it: "JusPrin uses this key for every chat. Replace it to use another one."
3. **Replacing.** An empty, focused field (2 px border-focus) "Paste the new key", with Check key, Cancel and "Keeps sk-ant-…a3F9". The saved key stays until the new one passes its check; Cancel keeps it.
4. **Checking.** The saved key stays visible, with "Checking…" and Cancel.
5. **Key rejected.** A circle-alert icon with "The provider rejected this key" (status-danger), and the key field outlined in status-danger with Replace and Remove. Below it: "Replace it with a working key, or remove it."
The provider segmented control (Anthropic / OpenAI / Other…) stays at the top. Each provider shows its own state.

## Facts (verified 2026-10-20)
- Keys are stored per provider in the app's settings file as `<provider>_api_key` (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/AgentConfiguration.cpp, api_key_item_for ~17 and load_provider_api_key ~40; the host already checks for a provider's key around line 103).
- The setup page always opens with an empty field: SetupApiKey in src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/components/Setup.tsx (`useState('')` ~100), so a saved key and no key look the same today.
- No dates are stored for keys. Don't show "added" or "last used" dates, and don't add storage for them unless Kenneth asks.

## How
- The host sends the page, per provider, only whether a key is saved and a display hint: the key's prefix up to and including its first "-" segment(s) the provider uses (e.g. "sk-ant-") plus its last 4 characters. Never send the full key to the web page.
- Add it through the bridge (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/bridge/protocol.ts and the host side) as a capability, not a protocol version bump.
- Remove deletes the provider's key (and whatever cached Agent uses it; follow how setup already rebuilds or clears the Agent). Replace keeps the old key until the new one passes the existing check. Rejected comes from the existing check path when the saved key fails.
- Tokens only (resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json through CSS variables); read agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md "Writing UI code" and agent-docs/jusprin/README.md first. Read agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md before touching files outside src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/.
- Tests for the host (a key's hint never contains more than prefix + last 4; Remove clears it) and for the page (each of the five states). Fail-first for any new guard (restore from a saved copy, never `git checkout`).
- Capture the five states in the review page or the built app, light and dark, and send Kenneth the pictures.
- Don't use Kenneth's real stored keys in tests, and make no live AI model calls without his approval. Never print a key. Commit only when he asks.

name: jusprin-claude-design-system-artifact
description: "The two Claude artifacts mirroring the Figma file JusPrin v2 (a Design System and a Design canvas): URLs, where the re-sync tools and backups live, how a re-sync is proven safe, what was measured on 2026-10-13, known gaps."

  originSessionId: 18e047ce-4892-4a44-8b70-c447eb34727c

---

Two private artifacts in Kenneth's Claude account mirror the Figma file
([[figma-jusprin-v2-file]]). Since 2026-10-20 these artifacts ARE the source of truth ([[design-source-is-claude-artifacts]]); edit them directly. The Figma re-sync steps below are history.

1. Design System: https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL (version 9)
   - `tokens.json` + `tokens.css`, 37 coded React components (`window.JusPrin`).
   - Each component card: every variant Figma draws, a Light and a Dark panel,
     then the coded component. The page lists them as one flat table in bundle
     order with code names; it draws no group headings.
   - `screens/<page>/<screen>.spec.txt` (166) + `screens/index.json`: plain
     files for agents, one resolved line per layer.
2. Design canvas "JusPrin v2": https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v
   (version 7): 10 pages with Figma's names in Figma's order, 198 artboards at
   their Figma x,y and in Figma's layer order, each drawn in the Light or Dark
   mode Figma sets on it; "… · Light & Dark" review frames are drawn whole.

Tools, reads and backups are durable now, outside the repo:
`~/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/figma-mirror/` — start with
its `README.md` (step-by-step re-sync). `published/` is an exact copy of what is
live; `backup-2026-10-13-before-reimport/` holds the earlier state with the
scripts that reproduce it byte for byte.

How Kenneth wants a re-sync done (2026-10-13): back up first, re-import, then
compare the backup with the new import so nothing already in sync regresses.
The method that worked, in order:
- rebuild from the old reads and require byte-identical output (proves the
  scripts);
- re-read Figma with the old script and diff the reads (proves Figma unchanged:
  all 14 files were identical);
- only then change scripts, and explain every file `compare_builds.py` reports;
- score every artboard against Figma's own page screenshots
  (`visual_compare.py`) and allow no artboard to score worse.
Result of that run: 0 artboards further from Figma, 36 closer; boards within 5
of Figma (0–255 scale) went from 99 to 122 of 186; all 37 cards and 163 of 166
spec files came out byte-identical; tokens matched Figma's variables exactly.

What the screenshot comparison caught that file checks could not: dark panels I
had added behind dark variants (Figma has none), frames forced dark by a "dark"
in their name (use Figma's `explicitVariableModes` instead), a frame half light
and half dark through a nested mode, sets whose background is a two-stop linear
gradient, Figma's GRID layout (children need their own positions), and small
frames centred in the 40px-minimum artboard instead of top-left.

Other traps: an absolutely positioned layer followed by in-flow siblings paints
over them in HTML (give the later siblings `position:relative`); Figma tints
icons with a mask plus a coloured rectangle; the Artifact tool's bulk read
prints small text files into context, so have a background agent do large
backups; a session scratchpad is wiped on restart — never keep the only copy of
tools there; when two reads of a page exist, keep the later one by timestamp.

Known gaps: photographs and 3D renders are flat placeholders (the 16 worst
scores are all such screens); radial and image fills are placeholders; Figma
stacks 12 dark screens on top of light ones on "Printer & Material Settings"
and the canvas keeps that; ProjectCard and PrinterCard variants are stacked in
Figma and laid out in a row on the canvas; "Add Printer Flow (Obsolete)" is not
read; Notice/Strip drifts a few px vertically.

Figma vs code differences Kenneth has not ruled on (the artifacts hold Figma's):
dark status colours (Figma #4CAF82 / #E07080 / #E8B84A, code #58B894 / #F07A8E /
#E9B960), `radius/full` 10 vs `pill` 9999, Button/Icon 32px vs 26px, Menu/Row
36px full-width hover vs the app's 32px inset rows
([[header-menu-values-kenneth-kept]]). See also [[figma-mcp-view-seat-limit]]
and [[claude-in-chrome-lives-in-claude-profile]].

Direct editing (2026-10-20): work on a copy of the live files (`figma-mirror/live-<date>` -> `work/`),
publish only the changed files, then rsync `work/` into `published/`. The canvas holds its own copy of the
design system in `project/ds/jusprin/` (tokens.css/json, components/bundle.*) — change both artifacts
together. `tools/composer/render.py` screenshots boards with headless Chrome (no type runtime needed);
measure natural board heights in the built-in browser and fix both the board file and canvas.json
(`resize_board.py`). `index.d.ts` must be published with contentType text/plain. The DS card height lives
in the `@dsCard height=` comment. Added then: `surface-raised-hover` (menu-row highlight, dark #3B3047) and
`component-composer-maxLines` (8); the new Composer is drawn by `tools/composer/composer_html.py`.

Publishing (2026-10-20, filament step): a publish is refused as "haven't viewed the latest version" unless this session did a plain `read` of the artifact url (path reads alone do not count). Headless Chrome hangs when another Chrome holds the default profile: pass `--user-data-dir=<tmp>` (render.py now does). MenuRow has `detail`, `detailTone: 'warning'` and `meta` since then.

**Trap found 2026-10-20 (turn line work):** `figma-mirror/tools/bundle.src.js`, `bundle.src.css` and `index.src.d.ts`
were STALE against the live Design System bundle (menu-row detail/meta and the Composer menus had been added
directly in the artifact). Running build_components.py or assembling from those sources regresses the live
bundle. Patch the live files (published/… copies, verified equal to the artifact by sha) and refresh the tools
sources from the patched result; `tools/composer/add_turn_line_boards.py` and the ChatTurnActivity card
were done that way. The DS page generates `tokens.css` itself: never publish it to the DS, only to the
canvas's `project/ds/jusprin/` copy. Adding a coded component = patch bundle.js (function + header list +
__EXPORTS__), bundle.css, index.d.ts (props + window typing), tokens.json, a hand-written
`components/<Name>/preview.html` card with `@dsCard height=` measured by rendering it with React from unpkg,
README.md's component list, and `design-system.json` lastChange in the last call.

Kenneth does not want to hear about obstacles encountered and solved during a
task — tooling that needed a workaround, a wrong first approach, a permission
that had to be re-requested, a window that had to be captured a different way.
Report the outcome and anything he must decide or act on.

Mention a solved problem only when it carries forward: it changes how he should
run something himself, it left residue in the repo or on his machine, it is
likely to recur and cost time later, or it revealed a real defect.

**Why:** Stated 2026-09-06 after a session summary spent a paragraph explaining
how a popup had to be screenshotted by its own window id and how the mouse
cursor was moved off the chevron. None of it changed anything for him.

**How to apply:** Before including a sentence about something that went wrong,
ask what he would do differently for having read it. If the answer is nothing,
cut it. This narrows the summaries described in [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]]
and applies to commit messages and PR descriptions as well as chat.

2026-10-17 repeat: a slice-failed summary listed "the real refusal text differs from the source; the skill quotes the shown text" under things Kenneth should know. It was a solved detail with no action for him; he called it showing off and a waste of his time. Test before listing a finding: does it change a decision or a step he takes? If not, leave it out of the summary (the report may keep it).

name: subagent-worktrees-create-manually
description: "Agent tool isolation:\"worktree\" cut worktrees from a stale base and SendMessage was disabled; create worktrees by hand on the intended commit and pass absolute paths"
metadata:

On 2026-09-08, three subagents launched with `isolation: "worktree"` got
worktrees at 095fb66576, an old commit with no JusPrin shell code, not the
branch tip they were told to expect. All three stopped correctly. SendMessage
was disabled in that session, so they could not be redirected; relaunching
was the only option.

**Why:** the isolation worktree is not cut from the current worktree's HEAD.
And `jusprin-newui` is rebased by other sessions while work is in flight, so
"base on newui" must be a specific commit, not a branch name.

**How to apply:** `git worktree add <path> -b <branch> <sha>` yourself, then
give the agent the absolute path and the expected SHA, and tell it to stop if
HEAD differs. Tell every agent the shell cwd may reset to the main checkout,
so all paths must be absolute. Before landing on `jusprin-newui`, read
`git reflog show jusprin-newui --date=relative`; if it moved in the last few
minutes another session is rebasing it. Land by cherry-pick, never
fast-forward, and expect your own commits to have new hashes afterwards.
See [[bash-cwd-resets-after-background]] and [[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]].

name: bash-cwd-resets-after-background
description: "The Bash tool's working directory silently reverts to the primary repo after a run_in_background command or a failed cd; worktree commands must cd explicitly or use absolute paths."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 3bfe66db-4c50-4102-b9b3-5ec3eab0060d
  modified: 2026-09-02T18:12:49.419Z
---

While working in a git worktree, a later `cmake --build build/arm64` and a
`git status` ran in `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin` (the main checkout)
instead of the worktree, so one build reported "no work to do" and a status
check looked as if every edit had been lost.

**Why:** After a `run_in_background` Bash call, and after a compound command
whose `cd` failed, the session cwd is the primary working directory again.
The tool result even says so, but it is easy to miss in a long session.

**How to apply:** In worktree sessions start every Bash command with
`cd <worktree> &&`, or use absolute paths everywhere (python patch scripts
with an absolute root are safest). Verify with `pwd` before trusting a
`git status` that looks wrong. See [[jusprin-worktree-build]].

name: background-bash-timeout-kills-builds
description: "A run_in_background Bash build dies at the tool timeout (ninja prints \"interrupted by user\", exit 130); launch long builds with nohup and watch the log instead"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 8c1e8dd3-1475-48e9-9398-2d5eaa424bab
  modified: 2026-09-14T19:01:34.576Z
---

A `cmake --build` started with the Bash tool's `run_in_background` is still
bound by that call's `timeout` (default 120 s, max 600 s). When it fires the
build log ends with `ninja: build stopped: interrupted by user.` and `exit=130`,
which looks like a human Ctrl-C but is the harness. Seen 2026-09-14 on a
725-step JusPrin rebuild.

**Why:** the notification says "completed" and the log shows no compiler
error, so it is easy to misread as a finished build; the changed files had not
compiled at all.

**How to apply:** for anything longer than a few minutes, start it detached
(`nohup sh -c "cmake --build … > log 2>&1; echo exit=\$? >> log" & disown`),
then arm a Monitor on the log that reports progress and the `exit=` line. Check
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' log` before trusting the result. Related:
[[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]], [[jusprin-worktree-build]].

description: "Publishing a design artifact arms a comment watch with auto-replies in that session; when several sessions work on the same artifact, each one answers the others' comments. Stop the watch after publishing unless Kenneth wants that session to handle comments."

On 2026-10-21 Kenneth found another session's canvas comments (a "Calibration · Printer & Filament" page) being auto-replied to and reported in this session, and asked how to make this session ignore it.

Cause: every publish to a Claude artifact arms a watch with comment auto-replies in the publishing session. Two sessions working on the JusPrin v2 canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v) or the Design System (https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL) both get every comment sent to Claude, wherever it is on the artifact.

**Why:** the wrong session answers a thread about work it doesn't know, and its reply can contradict the session that owns the boards.

**How to apply:** after a publish, stop the watch (ArtifactComments action "watch", on: false) unless Kenneth said this session owns the artifact's comments. Re-read the live artifact before publishing again, since another session may have published since. Related: [[jusprin-claude-design-system-artifact]], [[design-source-is-claude-artifacts]].

# JusPrin production documentation

This directory is the canonical starting point for production work on `jusprin-newui`. It preserves the durable product and engineering decisions from `jusprin-v2-poc` without importing the POC's temporary windows, probes, static mocks, generated evidence, or environment-gated startup paths.

Read these documents in order:

1. [Product definition](product-definition.md) — the human/agent boundary, required product surfaces, workflow, and visibility rules.
2. [Production architecture](architecture.md) — the selected native/WebView architecture, ownership rules, component boundaries, and implementation sequence.
3. [Engineering and verification method](engineering-method.md) — how to assess risk and what evidence is required before calling a feature complete.
4. [OrcaSlicer integration guide](orca-integration-guide.md) — known Orca behaviors, lifecycle traps, event and history constraints, and testing lessons.
5. [Fork stewardship](fork-stewardship.md) — required before changing any OrcaSlicer-owned file: where a seam belongs, why additive beats rewritten, how to leave a conflict that resolves correctly, and what evidence a change must record.
6. [Design system](design-system.md) — brand behavior, semantic UI tokens, typography, spacing, accessibility, and asset rules.
7. [POC reference](poc-reference.md) — exact pointers to the spike-only documents, code, commits, logs, screenshots, and generated brand artifacts left on `jusprin-v2-poc`.

## Governing decisions

- JusPrin is an AI-piloted 3D-printing product built on OrcaSlicer, not a replacement slicing engine.
- OrcaSlicer's C++ model, slicing pipeline, viewport, geometry operations, project serialization, and undo stack remain authoritative.
- The production application stays native C++/wxWidgets/OpenGL. The Agent conversation uses a local React/TypeScript application inside `wxWebView`.
- JavaScript renders state and submits typed commands; it never owns editable Orca project state.
- When logic could live in either C++ or a React page, it goes in the page unless there is a strong reason for C++: it touches Orca state, enforces a limit or boundary the app must guarantee, has to work without a page, or needs a thread or lifetime the page lacks. See [Where logic goes](architecture.md#where-logic-goes-the-page-first).
- Product policy lives in fork-owned files. OrcaSlicer-owned files receive only small, product-neutral, additive seams — every line changed there is a line this fork re-resolves at every rebase.
- The user owns physical facts, object meaning, desired outcomes, privacy and legal decisions, and starting consequential physical actions.
- The production branch must not import experimental POC behavior merely because it demonstrated feasibility. Use the POC as evidence and reimplement through stable production boundaries.

## Writing UI code

Rules for anyone, human or agent, adding or changing a JusPrin surface. They
exist because every value that is typed by hand drifts from the design system and
from the other side of the app within weeks; today's guards catch most of it, but
only if the code goes through the token file in the first place.

1. **Never type a color, radius, font, or control size.** Every one comes
   from `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`. Native code reads it
   through `ShellTheme`: `palette(dark)` for color, `metrics()` for radii,
   spacing, and per-component sizes, `font(role)` for type. A stock
   `wxStaticText`, `wxTextCtrl`, or OrcaSlicer `Button` is
   dressed through `Shell/ShellRecipes.hpp`, never by calling its setters
   with literals. The Agent page uses only `var(--…)`: `--<group>-<name>` for
   color, `--radius-<name>`, `--font-<role>`, `--font-code`, and
   `--button-<recipe>-padding`.
2. **If the value you need has no token, add the token first.** Put it in
   the JSON, extend the guard in `tests/brand/test_brand_tokens.cpp` so a
   later edit cannot silently move it, then read it from code. Do not write
   the number "for now": the guards cannot see a literal that is already
   there, and the next reader cannot tell a decision from an accident. A
   value that exists in the design artifacts but not in the roles or scales is a design
   decision to raise, not a reason to type it.
3. **Layout spacing may stay literal, on the scale.** Padding between
   regions, gaps, and margins use 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, or 48 DIP.
   Control padding is not layout spacing; it comes from a button recipe.
4. **Pick the nearest role, never a bespoke size.** The roles are the whole
   type system. Bold at a body or label size is a role of its own; if a
   surface seems to need a size that no role has, see rule 2.
5. **The design system wins when it and the code disagree.** The two Claude
   artifacts are the source of truth (Kenneth, 2026-10-20; Figma is
   retired): the Design System
   (https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL) and the "JusPrin v2"
   canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v). Change the
   token file to match, or, when the code's value is the one to keep, change
   the artifact first. Do not trust old commit messages about either.
6. **Run the guards before calling UI work done:** `brand_tokens_tests`,
   `shell_theme_tests`, and `npm test` in `AgentUI`. Then look at the surface
   in the running app; the guards prove the code went through the tokens,
   not that the result looks right.
7. **Upstream files are off limits for style.** OrcaSlicer's own screens are
   retinted through the hooks `BrandPalette.cpp` installs and nothing else;
   see [Fork stewardship](fork-stewardship.md). Their radii and fonts stay
   OrcaSlicer's until the surface is replaced.

description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.

**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and

all. **The cause was not isolated** — reuse and the stale helper were not separated, so
treat this as a recipe, not an explanation. `rm -rf` and recreate the scratch `$HOME`,
`pkill -f jusprin-mcp`, then run; if the handshake wait appears anyway, kill it early
rather than assuming the change under test broke the bridge.

**One decision is yours: when a saved key counts as "rejected".** The board shows the saved key being checked, but nothing in the app checks a saved key today. I made a key show as rejected after the provider refuses it in a real chat (a 401 or 403). That flag lasts until the app quits or the key is replaced or removed. I did not add a check when the screen opens, because that would cost a live request every time someone opens it. As built, "Checking…" (state 4) appears while a replacement key is being checked, and the saved key stays on screen during that check. One gap: if the provider refuses the key in the printer panel's chat, the screen won't show it as rejected, because that panel can't tell which provider's key failed. If you'd rather check the saved key when the screen opens, it's a small change.

**What changed**
- **What the page gets:** the app sends it each provider's hint and a rejected flag, never the key. The hint is the provider's standard start plus the last 4 characters, e.g. `sk-ant-…a3F9`. A key too short to keep 8 characters hidden shows no last 4. This was added as a new `saved_keys` capability with two messages, `setup_keys` and `setup_remove_key`, with no protocol version bump.
- **Remove** deletes the key from the settings file and saves at once. If that was the provider chats use by default, the default moves to a provider that still has a key and the Agent is rebuilt on it. If no key is left, the panel goes back to "not set up".
- **Replace** keeps the old key until the new one passes the existing check. If the new key fails, the old one stays and the error shows under the field.
- **Page:** the five states, with "Paste" inside the field and the board's wording. Styles use design tokens only.

content.text:
Mostly compliant. Colours, spacing, corner radii and text styles all come from tokens. Most sizes are typed as plain numbers, but that is normal on the canvas because its token stylesheet has no size variables (the design system's own component boards do the same), and almost all of them match a token. The one real exception is the key field itself: it is 36 px tall with 12 px side padding, and no token gives those values.

**What I checked:** I listed every literal value in the board's styles and compared each against `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json` and the canvas's own `tokens.css`.

| Literal on the board | Token it matches | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Segmented control 30 px tall, 2 px padding | `segmented.height` 30, `segmented.padding` 2 | Matches |
| Check key button 34 px tall | `button.primary`: 8 px top and bottom padding around 18 px body-small-bold text | Matches |
| Icons 16 px | `button.icon.iconSize` 16 | Matches |
| Borders 1 px, focus border 2 px | `fieldSearch.borderWidth` 1, `focusBorderWidth` 2 | Matches |
| State cards 429 px wide | `agentPane.width` 429 | Matches |
| `#F5F5F5` backdrop, 922×984 frame | The artboard around the design, not app UI; every canvas board has it | Not UI |
| **Key field 36 px tall, 12 px side padding** | **None** | **Off the token system** |

**The key field doesn't use the design system's own secret field.** The canvas has a component board, `ds-field-secret.dc.html` ("Field/Secret"), for exactly this kind of input. It is 26 px tall (`field.height`) with 8 px side padding (`field.paddingX`), and it shows the value in the code text style. The new board drew its own field at 36 px with 12 px padding instead. Its placeholder also uses the body-small text style, while the field token's text style is body.

Two smaller things I noticed:
- **Links:** "Paste", "Replace" and "Remove" are drawn as bare text, not as the Link button component (26 px tall, 4 px side padding).
- **Segments:** in a 30 px track the segments come out 26 px tall, not the 24 px `segmentHeight` token. The design system's own Segmented Control board draws them the same way, so this comes from that board, not this one.

**My code doesn't follow Field/Secret either.** I built the field at 34 px (26 px link buttons plus 4 px above and below) with 12 px left padding. That avoided the off-token 36 but still isn't the system's field.

**Decision for you: which height the key field should be.**
- **Use Field/Secret (my recommendation).** The field becomes 26 px with 8 px padding, and I change both the board and the code to match. The 26 px link buttons fit inside it exactly, so no new token is needed.
- **Keep the board's 36 px.** That needs a new component token for a taller key field, added to the token file and its guard test first, as the UI-code rules require.

Either way I would also draw the three links as the Link button component on the board. Nothing on the canvas or in the code has changed during this check.

Use Field/Secret. 
afterward, test the app, cpature screenshots for me to review
I'll switch the key field to the Field/Secret sizes in the code and on the canvas board, then rebuild and capture the app.

"""Makes room for the taller Composer: the content area just above the Composer frame shrinks and clips instead of
running under the box or pushing it out of the pane. Usage: fit_content.py <canvas project dir> <board>..."""
import re, sys
from pathlib import Path
from htmlfrag import element_at, TAG
proj = Path(sys.argv[1])
for name in sys.argv[2:]:
    f = proj / name; s = f.read_text()
    i = s.index('data-n="Composer box"')
    stack = []
    for m in TAG.finditer(s):
        if m.start() >= i: break
        close, tag, selfclose = m.group(1), m.group(2), m.group(3)
        if tag in ('path', 'circle', 'rect', 'line', 'polyline', 'polygon', 'img') or selfclose: continue
        if close: stack.pop()

    frame, pane = stack[-2], stack[-3]  # stack[-1] is the Composer box itself
    # the frame's previous sibling inside the pane
    j = s.index('>', pane) + 1; prev = None
    while j < frame:
        a, b = element_at(s, j); prev = a; j = b
    end = s.index('>', prev)
    tag = s[prev:end]
    m = re.search(r'style="([^"]*)"', tag); st = m.group(1)
